newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - HRW harvest progresses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - HRW harvest progresses.

text.p: Farmers began cutting hard red winter wheat in Montana this week and early yields and protein varied widely across the state, cash grain dealers said.
"The stuff we saw today was about 61.5 pounds (per bushel)," a northern Montana dealer said. We consider 60 pounds or better pretty good. Protein was close to 13 percent."
Further east, heat and moisture stress late in the growing season led to lower protein content but overall quality was better than some had expected, a southeast Montana merchandiser said.
"We're bringing a lot of new crop in today but mostly for storage," the dealer said. "The new crop is looking pretty good. It's not the proteins we had last year. It's closer to 11.5 percent."

Bids for dark northern spring wheat were down slightly in reaction to a modest decline in MGE spring wheat futures. Harvest was expected to begin in the southern wheat belt within a week, dealers said.
